  mesh-serve now has the endpoints that replace the manual six-step loop, all 
  exposed                                                                     
  ( visibility: 'public' , so a site may gate them):                          
                                                                              
  •  catalog.declare  — create/edit a part and how it builds, no repo clone,  
  no version                                                                  
  •  builder.import_repo  — read a repository's  mesh.json  once into part    
  rows                                                                        
  •  builder.release_part  — pull, mint the next version, publish, build, emit
  •  builder.release_repo  — every part one repository declares, kernels first
  •  cdn.compose  now takes  rolling: true , and a rolling release re-composes
  itself and                                                                  
  moves its sites when a part it names is released                            
                                                                              
  No screen calls any of them. That is the whole issue, and it is the standing
  complaint:                                                                  
                                                                              
  │ what do you mean 'Running the full cycle now' like what are you doing?    
  │ there needs to be a                                                       
  │ button on the ui to do this. stuff like this is what i need.              
                                                                              
  ## What to build, in mesh-core                                              
                                                                              
  Catalog console:                                                            
                                                                              
  • Import a repository — a form taking a repository URL and an optional ref, 
  calling                                                                     
   builder.import_repo , showing the parts it declared. Leave the ref empty by
  default: absent                                                             
  means the repository's own default branch.                                  
  • Per part: a Release button ( builder.release_part , with a                
  patch/minor/major choice) showing                                           
  the version it minted and the digest it built.                              
  • Per repository: Release all ( builder.release_repo ), rendering the       
  released list and the                                                       
  failed list separately — failures are reported, not thrown, and there will  
  be some.                                                                    
  • A part's declaration (entry, branch, kernel range, requires) is editable  
  and saved with                                                              
   catalog.declare . This is what replaces editing  mesh.json  by hand.

   src/catalog/contracts/part.contract.ts  for the exact shapes — the doc

    bring-up runs the whole pipeline, one function per step
    
    It stopped after import. Now it goes through to a hostname serving a release:
    
      ensureUser / ensureOrganization / ensureMembership / issueTicket
      assignServices    the fleet tells the node to run catalog, builder, cdn
      importRepository  mesh.json read once, into part rows
      releaseRepository pull, mint a version, publish, build — kernels first
      composeRelease    ranges in, digests out, marked rolling
      ensureSite        grants DERIVED from what the release calls
      deploySite        one field
    
    Every one is exported and idempotent, so a step can be run alone.
    
    grantsFor derives the site's mesh list from release.requires rather than a
    hand-written list. cdn.deploy refuses a release calling an ungranted contract,
    so a maintained-by-hand list goes stale exactly when a part is added — the
    moment somebody is least able to guess why the deploy was refused. Events are
    derived the same way, at the gate the collection's own find has, which is what
    makes a console list live rather than a snapshot.
    
    --identity-only and --import-only stop early. A build failure stops before
    compose, because composing on a partial release fails again, more confusingly,
    several steps from the build that actually broke.

    the generic CRUD path cannot write there — it failed with 'user not found' on an
    id just read successfully, and the failure was swallowed by a .catch. The role
    is asserted in the meta, and callerFor says plainly why that is not a smaller
    claim: any peer that can join can construct any meta. See D6.
    
    Adds test/api/visibility.test.ts. visibility is read in exactly one place,
    describeExposure, so 'internal' means not-routable-over-HTTP and does not mean
    not-callable: bring-up reads user.find_one with no meta at all. The two tests
